Title: Govt aiming to increase cocoa plantations to 10,000ha by 2030
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Only 281 tonnes of the 294,697 tonnes of cocoa beans ground in Malaysia last year were produced locally, says Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad.
The remaining 294,416 tonnes were imported.
She said the government aimed to increase the country's cocoa planted areas to 10,000ha by 2030 from the current 6,939ha.
She said this was in line with the National Agricommodity Policy 2030, which targets raising dried cocoa bean yields from 0.2 tonnes per hectare last year to 0.56 tonnes per hectare by 2030.
"Through the target of expanding cultivation to 10,000ha by 2030 and efforts to increase productivity, the government aims to gradually increase the contribution of local cocoa beans to the needs of the grinding industry," she said during Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
She was responding to a question from Bakri Jamaluddin (PN-Tangga Batu), who asked for the government's concrete targets to raise local cocoa bean production and the percentage of import reduction targeted by 2030.
"The government's goal is not merely to reduce dependence on imports, but also to redevelop the country's upstream cocoa sector, increase smallholders' incomes, create job opportunities and ensure Malaysia's cocoa industry remains competitive and sustainable," she said.
Noraini said 3,295 cocoa smallholders had received agricultural inputs to increase the productivity of existing crops.
The ministry's efforts include expanding cultivation, rehabilitating existing farms, using research and technology to raise productivity, working more closely with the grinding industry and producing premium beans such as single-origin and fine-flavour cocoa.
Noraini said a large part of the country's cocoa exports last year came from value-added downstream products.
Cocoa butter alone was worth RM7.24 billion, followed by cocoa powder at RM4.23 billion and chocolate at RM1.85 billion.
She said the number of local chocolate entrepreneurs under the Malaysian Cocoa Board rose from 242 in 2021 to 270 last year.
Their annual sales increased by 228 per cent, from RM5.55 million to RM18.21 million.
From January to August this year, 280 entrepreneurs recorded sales of RM18.31 million and production of 353.04 tonnes, surpassing last year's total sales.
On the board's target of a cocoa yield of 1,300kg per hectare a year, she said several factors were involved.
"However, achieving a yield of 1,300kg per hectare a year depends on several factors, including the age and condition of the trees, the type of clone used, soil suitability, farm management practices and the level of pest and disease control," she said.
In October, Noraini had said Malaysia needed to
boost local cocoa bean production
to reduce reliance on imports, as the processing industry depended heavily on foreign supplies.

Title: 6-year-olds may face compulsory Year One entry from 2029
Article:
SEPANG: The Education Ministry plans to make enrolment in Year One compulsory for 6-year-olds from 2029, following an optional early-entry arrangement for parents in 2027 and 2028.
Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said the three-year transition period would allow the ministry to ensure that preparations involving the curriculum, teacher training, infrastructure and classrooms were carried out continuously before the policy became mandatory.
He said preparations had begun this year to ensure the policy was implemented smoothly and sustained until its objectives were achieved.
"When we make it compulsory in 2029, it means the effort will run from today, 2026, until 2029.
"We do not want an initiative that has been planned to eventually stall before it is fully implemented," he said in a media briefing.
Azam said the ministry was confident it had the capacity to implement the policy, citing existing resources and the use of the Industrialised Building System (IBS), which could enable additional classrooms to be built within three months, depending on requirements.
The ministry also had several mechanisms to manage pupil placement, including operating schools in two sessions and redistributing pupils to schools with lower enrolment.
He said the curriculum had also taken into account the learning needs of 6-year-olds, while teacher training would be adjusted to prepare educators to handle pupils of that age.
He said the policy was not merely about accelerating children's entry into primary school, but also about responding to changing educational challenges and making the most of children's potential at a younger age.
"We are moving towards an ageing nation and cannot afford to delay preparations for future changes, including technological developments and climate change.
"Even at a young age, children now have access to a wide range of knowledge and information. Their potential must therefore be harnessed," he said.
Azam said the approach was also intended to ensure equal access to and equity in education for all children, rather than having opportunities depend on specific arrangements such as the accelerated learning classes introduced previously.
He said making Year One enrolment compulsory for six-year-olds would also require amendments to the Education Act 1996.
On the initial optional arrangement, he said parents' response had been mixed, although demand had increased, including appeals from parents who had seen the ministry's preparations.
He said appeals would be assessed based on classroom readiness and schools' placement capacity before decisions were made.
The ministry had also drawn up initial projections for additional classrooms, textbooks and teachers should applications increase in 2028.
As of Sept 30, the ministry had received 73,498 applications from the 6-year-old cohort for Year One enrolment, compared with 418,151 applications from the seven-year-old cohort.
This brought the total number of applications for Year One registration for the 2027 academic calendar to 491,649.

Title: MoE to begin planning dedicated autism classes next year
Article:
SEPANG: The Education Ministry will begin planning dedicated classes for autistic pupils next year as part of efforts to provide more specialised learning tailored to their needs.
Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said the initiative was prompted by the growing number of pupils with autism and the need for a more focused approach to their education.
"Based on the views of special education experts, autism requires specific treatment or initiatives," he said at a media briefing.
He said ministry data showed an increase in the number of pupils with autism, warranting greater attention to their educational needs.
The ministry was also planning to expand special education classrooms to accommodate the growing number of pupils with special educational needs, although this would require additional teachers to support the expansion.
Azam said the Special Education Division would coordinate the planning and implementation of these initiatives.
Education (School Operations Sector) deputy director-general Datuk Zainal Abas said enrolment of pupils with special educational needs had been rising annually, partly due to greater public awareness and more parents seeking assessments for their children.
He said the ministry provided two education pathways for these pupils: special education schools and the Special Education Integration Programme (PPKI) in mainstream schools.
"More parents are becoming aware and bringing their children for assessments to determine whether they have special educational needs.
"The ministry has been working on a special education planning framework since last year, including the construction of additional classrooms," he said.
Under the planned expansion, each PPKI classroom would ideally accommodate seven pupils, supported by a special education teacher and a teaching assistant. However, some existing classes currently had between seven and 10 pupils.
Zainal said the ministry was also developing dedicated classes for autistic pupils, who were currently placed alongside pupils with Down syndrome and other learning difficulties under the PPKI.
He said the move recognised the different learning requirements of autistic pupils and would complement existing initiatives, including the Permata programme.
The Permata programme is a specialised suite of early childhood, special needs, gifted, arts, and youth initiatives designed to support children and youth from birth through adulthood.
On enrolment among younger pupils, Zainal said 9,997 applications had been recorded for seven-year-olds under the primary school PPKI programme, compared with 656 for six-year-olds.
He said admission also depended on pupils' readiness, particularly their ability to manage basic self-care independently.
"Although each class has a teacher and a teaching assistant to support pupils, they must still have basic self-care abilities," he said.
He added that the 2026 Preschool Curriculum would introduce two additional learning areas for pupils with special educational needs, bringing the total from six to eight.
The additional components were intended to better prepare these pupils for their transition to Year One.
Meanwhile, Azam said the country's first Special Education Sports School in Bandar Enstek, Negeri Sembilan, was expected to begin enrolling Form One pupils next year.
He said construction was about 98 to 99 per cent complete, with the handover to the ministry pending the Public Works Department's readiness.
"We had planned for the handover to take place this year, but we will have to see whether the department is ready. Student intake may therefore begin next year," he said.
The school would provide pupils with special educational needs opportunities to develop their sporting potential and contribute to the country's achievements internationally, including at the Paralympic Games.
Azam said these pupils should have equal access to quality education and opportunities to develop into well-rounded individuals, in line with the National Education Philosophy.

Title: Maybank shares rise on strong 3Q performance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd's (Maybank)  shares rose on Tuesday following the group's strong performance in the third quarter (3Q) ended Sept 30, 2026.
At lunch break, the counter rose 19 sen to RM10.08, with 5.63 million shares traded.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia yesterday, Maybank said its net profit for 3Q rose to RM2.74 billion from RM2.62 billion in the same quarter last year.
The result was supported by lower impairment losses, along with stronger performance from its Islamic banking and insurance/takaful service businesses, it said.
However, Maybank said revenue fell to RM14.56 billion from RM16.60 billion previously.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, the bank's net profit improved to RM7.91 billion from RM7.83 billion, while revenue declined to RM45.55 billion from RM50.55 billion previously, it said.
In a research note, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said Maybank's results were in line with its expectations.
"(However) we remain cautious about Maybank's near-term net interest margin outlook, as sluggish deposit growth and an elevated loan-to-deposit ratio continues to intensify funding competition," it said.
HLIB maintained its "Hold" recommendation on Maybank with an unchanged target price of RM10.50.

Title: Trump tells Justice Department to seek death penalty for child killers, rapists
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump has directed the Department of Justice to seek the death penalty for those who murder children, as well as for rapists and human traffickers, Sputnik/RIA Novosti reported.
"In a few moments, I will sign a presidential directive ordering the Department of Justice to seek the death penalty for child murderers, as well as rapists and human traffickers who kill their victims," ​​he said at a press conference at the Justice Department.
Trump also instructed the Attorney General to expedite the execution of death sentences.
"Once juries have spoken, capital punishment will be swift and certain," he emphasised.
The statement comes against the backdrop of a decision by California Governor Gavin Newsom to commute the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the state's death row to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.
He explained that the death penalty was incompatible with the values ​​of California, where no executions had actually taken place since January 2006.

Title: PetChem swings back to RM179mil profit in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd swung to a net profit of RM179 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from a net loss of RM289 million a year earlier, despite softer product prices.
Revenue for the quarter rose 12.3 per cent to RM7.62 billion from RM6.79 billion in the corresponding quarter last year.
Higher sales volumes supported this, partially offsetting lower average product prices, particularly urea.
The group recorded a pre-tax profit of RM256 million, reversing from a pre-tax loss of RM296 million a year earlier.
However, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) declined to RM942 million from RM1.32 billion previously, as weaker product spreads across its portfolios outweighed improvements in operating costs.
Its Ebitda margin narrowed to 12.4 per cent from 16.7 per cent in the second quarter, while plant utilisation stood at 73 per cent.
Petronas Chemicals' utilisation rate was lower than the 90 per cent recorded in the corresponding quarter last year.
This was mainly due to increased maintenance activities at its olefins plant in Kertih and planned statutory turnaround activities at its methanol plant in Labuan.
Managing director and chief executive officer Mazuin Ismail said the group's lower earnings reflected softer overall product prices, particularly urea, following increased export availability from China.
"Despite the scheduled turnaround activities at our methanol plant in Labuan and interruptions at the olefins plant in Kertih, sales volume increased during the quarter, driven by higher contribution from Pengerang operations and strategic sourcing," he said in a statement.
For the nine months, Petronas Chemicals recorded a net profit attributable to shareholders of RM994 million, reversing from a net loss of RM1.39 billion in the corresponding period last year.
Net profit for the period stood at RM1.07 billion compared with a net loss of RM1.32 billion previously.
Revenue for the nine-month period rose eight per cent to RM22.54 billion from RM20.88 billion, driven by higher average product prices, partially offset by the stronger ringgit and lower sales volumes.
The group declared a dividend of six sen per share for the nine-month period, compared with three sen per share in the corresponding period last year.
Petronas Chemicals said the chemicals market will continue to be shaped by geopolitical uncertainties, shifting trade policies and supply-demand imbalances.
It expects prices of olefins and derivatives to remain under pressure amid regional oversupply, while geopolitical tensions could contribute to volatility in feedstock and freight costs.
Fertiliser demand is expected to be supported by seasonal agricultural requirements, food security priorities and import demand, while methanol prices are expected to remain broadly stable.
Meanwhile, demand for specialty chemicals is expected to remain soft, particularly in the construction, automotive and consumer goods sectors, with seasonal weakness anticipated in the fourth quarter.

Title: B40 students account for 72.5pct of TVET enrolment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Students from B40 households make up 72.5 per cent of enrolment at polytechnics and community colleges nationwide, highlighting efforts to widen access to technical and vocational education and training (TVET).
Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim said the institutions had a combined enrolment of 103,388 students in 2025.
He said polytechnics and community colleges offered 699 programmes, ranging from certificate to bachelor's degree level, allowing students to progress academically within the TVET system.
The programmes covered fields including civil, mechanical, electrical and marine engineering, information technology, networking, cybersecurity and manufacturing.
"These programmes cater to students' potential and abilities," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Adam Adli was responding to a question from Mohd Hasnizan Harun (PN-Hulu Selangor) on declining participation in the pure science stream and government efforts to increase students' interest in science-related subjects.
He said the institutions had also helped Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) leavers from humanities and professional arts (KSI) streams transition into science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields.
Of the 31,873 graduates produced last year, 25,571, or 80.2 per cent, came from KSI streams.
"Of these graduates, 7,873 completed engineering programmes and another 7,194 graduated in technology," he said.
Adam Adli said the range of programmes and progression pathways allowed students to further their studies according to their abilities and potential.
He said the high proportion of B40 students also reflected the government's commitment to inclusive education under its TVET for All agenda.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MHB's Q3 net profit jumps 29pct to RM37mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Marine and Heavy Engineering Holdings Bhd's (MHB) net profit rose 29 per cent to RM36.39 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), from RM28.2 million a year earlier, on the back of higher revenue.
Revenue for the quarter increased 35.8 per cent to RM692.23 million from RM509.86 million previously, with the increase contributed by both its heavy engineering and marine segments.
Earnings per share rose to 2.30 sen from 1.80 sen a year earlier.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, MHB's net profit more than doubled to RM111.27 million from RM50.56 million a year earlier.
Revenue for the cumulative period surged 58.3 per cent to RM2.2 billion from RM1.39 billion.
Managing director and chief executive officer Mohd Nazir Mohd Nor said the global energy landscape continues to be driven by a sustained focus on energy security and supply resilience.
This supports investment across offshore oil and gas, liquefied natural gas (LNG) and related energy infrastructure markets.
"While geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, uncertainties surrounding project development and the energy transition may affect market dynamics and timelines, industry activity is expected to remain steady, presenting opportunities for the group.
"Amid these market conditions, the heavy engineering segment remains focused on
delivering its ongoing projects effectively, while selectively pursuing opportunities in targeted growth segments, both domestically and internationally," he said in a statement.
Mohd Nazir said the marine segment is expected to operate in a competitive environment shaped by evolving global shipping dynamics and ongoing geopolitical developments.
He noted that the growing LNG carrier fleet and sustained LNG trade activity are expected to support demand for repair and maintenance services.
Ongoing floater conversion projects are also expected to contribute to the group's financial performance.

Title: Bigger allocation proposed to upgrade school PA systems
Article:
SEPANG: The Education Ministry is proposing a substantial allocation to upgrade public address (PA) systems in schools amidst complaints of audio disruptions during the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) Bahasa Melayu Listening Test.
Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said the proposed allocation would strengthen schools' audio facilities and prevent similar incidents from recurring.
He acknowledged reports of technical issues during the examination but said the incidents reported so far appeared to be isolated rather than widespread.
He said the existing examination management structure, involving the Examinations Board, state education departments, district education offices and school principals, had established standard operating procedures to address such issues.
"School examination managers and state examination managers should assess their respective needs and take the necessary action.
"However, what went viral yesterday was not a widespread issue, but involved isolated cases," he said during a media briefing.
Azam said the Examinations Board had been instructed by Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek and himself to review the reported incidents and ensure appropriate action was taken.
He said he had previously proposed an allocation to improve school PA systems but it was not yet implemented.
"I have raised the proposal again.
"I cannot disclose the amount yet, but it is a substantial sum intended to help schools improve their PA systems," he said.
He added that complaints about audio quality could also arise from students having difficulty understanding pronunciation, particularly in English, rather than technical faults with the equipment itself.
He said similar concerns had been raised two to three years ago, highlighting the need to assess students' ability to understand spoken words during listening tests.
On the investigation into the latest complaints, Azam said the Examinations Board director had independent authority under the Education Act 1996 to administer examinations and make decisions relating to examination awards.
He said the board submitted a report to the education minister, with any further action to be communicated following an assessment.
Earlier today, the Examinations Board said it would conduct further investigations into allegations of technical problems with the audio during the SPM Bahasa Melayu Listening Test.
The board said this in response to complaints on social media platform Threads, where candidates alleged that the audio had repeatedly cut out, disrupting their ability to complete the examination.
"Thank you for bringing this to our attention. The Examinations Board takes note of the matter and further investigations will follow," it said in its response.
Earlier, a Threads user identified as teysszzzzz appealed to Fadhlina to allow candidates to retake the test following the alleged audio disruptions.
The user claimed that the audio had played intermittently and that no action was taken by the chief invigilator despite the problem occurring during the examination.
Another Threads user, annur_aaa, also alleged that audio problems had occurred at her school's examination hall, prompting candidates to raise their hands to alert invigilators.
She said the matter had been brought to the chief invigilator's attention but claimed no action was taken at the time.

Title: RHB e-payments surge 37pct to 1.2bil transactions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Banking Group recorded more than 1.2 billion e-payment transactions across Payments Network Malaysia Sdn Bhd's (PayNet) national payments network between July 2025 and June 2026.
This represents a 37 per cent increase year-on-year.
The volume rose from 886 million transactions in the corresponding period a year earlier, marking the highest growth among Malaysian banks.
Of the total, 536.8 million transactions were payments made by RHB customers, while 676.7 million were payments received into RHB accounts by individuals and businesses.
The increase reflects a shift among customers and merchants towards faster and more convenient payment methods, spanning everyday activities such as retail purchases, bill payments, online transactions and business collections.
RHB said the growth in transactions reflected the increasing use of digital payments as customers and businesses increasingly adopted electronic payment methods.
The group was named winner of the E-Payments Excellence Award (Bank) at PayNet's Malaysian E-Payments Excellence Awards (MEEA) 2026, marking its second consecutive year of recognition.
RHB Group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Rashid Mohamad said digital payments were fast becoming the preferred way for customers to manage their daily transactions, with the 37 per cent growth reflecting that shift.
He said whether paying for a meal, making an online purchase, settling bills or collecting business payments, customers expected transactions to be quick, simple and reliable.
"As these expectations continue to evolve, our focus is on making it easier for customers and businesses to transact, while ensuring they can do so with confidence.
"Being recognised for the second consecutive year reflects the role that digital payments now play in everyday life, and it encourages us to keep raising the standard of service we provide as we work towards becoming the Best Service Bank," he said in a statement.
The group became the first bank in Malaysia to enable merchants to accept DuitNow Pay for online and recurring payments through RHB Pay, its unified online payment gateway.
The enhancement gives businesses greater flexibility in collecting payments while providing customers with a seamless payment experience across different transaction types.
RHB Pay will progressively support additional payment options, including Direct Debit, DuitNow QR and e-wallets.
The group said the recognition reinforced its direction as digital payments became increasingly embedded in the way people lived, worked and conducted business.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervention in abrupt board reversal
Article:
NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, drawing approval from Wall Street and opposition from US lawmakers.
Huang's comeback caps a whirlwind week of events that roiled markets and tore through the AI ecosystem that has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.
But the board's about-face - less than a week after Chair Harvey Jones said Nvidia would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behavior was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct - raises questions about its independence, governance experts said, even as the company's investigation remains unfinished.
Huang's comeback boosted Wall Street and sent Nvidia's shares soaring. The stock closed up 31.5 per cent, adding nearly US$1 trillion in market value, vaulting the chipmaker back to the position of the second-biggest company by market value after Apple.
The gains were not enough, however, to erase all losses since Huang's resignation on Nov 12.
Nvidia said in a statement that based on US government input the board was confident that "Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk," a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC.
Huang said in a statement that he was honored to return and "can't wait to get back to work." He returned to company headquarters to cheers from employees.
"Jensen's return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management. "Certain executives are going to be held to different standards if you are perceived to be a one of one," he said, adding Huang would still have to answer "some tough questions from Congress."
Lawmakers across party lines strongly objected to Huang's reinstatement and called on Congress to pass the Chip Security Act, a bill that seeks to stop legally exported advanced chips from being diverted to China, where their sales are restricted.
US Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Trump was "putting his own financial interests... before our national security," while Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said Huang's return "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips."
TRUMP'S SUPPORT FOR HUANG
Huang returned at the strong urging of Trump, industry leaders including Elon Musk, and some investors.
His departure had reverberated from Silicon Valley to Taipei. A petition calling for his reinstatement drew more than 180,000 signatures, underscoring the unusually strong support for an executive who stepped down amid controversy.
"I believe my intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back," Trump told CNBC.
Trump owns between US$11 million and US$55 million in Nvidia stock, according to a Reuters review of his annual financial disclosure for 2025 and share trading disclosures for 2026.
Monday's surge in Nvidia shares could have boosted Trump's net worth by as much as US$17 million.
A White House spokesperson said Trump's stock and bond portfolio was independently managed by third-party financial institutions and neither the president nor any member of his family had any ability to direct or influence how the portfolio was invested.
Nvidia's board did not mention Huang's affairs. Apart from Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman who is accused of having ties with Beijing, Huang is accused of having had intimate relationships with at least two Nvidia employees.
Jensen Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologised, but has not publicly addressed the individual alleged relationships in detail. China has denied the espionage allegations. Attempts by Reuters to reach Alice Huang have been unsuccessful.
CHINA IS KEY TO NVIDIA
Huang's return comes as Nvidia faces heightened scrutiny in Washington over the flow of advanced AI chips to China.
US authorities have tightened licensing rules for some chip shipments and overseas data centers serving Chinese companies, while lawmakers are preparing to question Huang, who has pushed for greater access to the Chinese market.
Huang has agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing on December 3, the Senate Banking Committee said. Huang's personal spokesperson declined to comment.
Trump told CNBC that he had urged Nvidia to continue reviewing its compliance with US export controls to ensure it was adequately protecting national security.
Trump, who visited Shenzhen last week, said he had spoken to Chinese President Xi Jinping about Huang.
Huang's exit from Nvidia threatened its business in China, Reuters reported on Monday, with some customers there cancelling or hesitating to place orders, jeopardizing billions in revenue.
The US on Monday added Alice Huang's former employer Megaspeed and Alibaba's Singapore subsidiary, which has business ties to the cloud firm at the center of the Nvidia scandal, to its trade blacklist.
Alibaba said allegations the subsidiary had diverted chips subject to US export restrictions were "erroneous," while Megaspeed has previously said it conducted legitimate and lawful business, including complying with US export controls.
Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Tuesday the city-state would continue its investigation into Megaspeed.
US and Singapore law enforcement conducted an onsite visit in 2025 and interviewed Alice Huang.
The Nvidia board has formed a committee to investigate whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Huang and another committee focused on national security and export controls.
The company is also facing multiple investigations over issues ranging from potential accounting irregularities to suspected chip smuggling, and a shareholder lawsuit accusing the company and Huang of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No suitable alternative yet to Sedition Act, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has yet to identify a suitable alternative to the Sedition Act 1948, despite Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's disagreement with the law.
Anwar said there was currently no alternative legislation to address disputes, particularly those involving race relations.
He said the Act's introduction during the tenure of the second prime minister, the late Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, reflected the leadership's emphasis on preserving racial harmony.
"That is why the leadership of Abdul Razak and former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman was very hard and firm on this matter, to the point of leading to the Sedition Act.
"There are many views on the problems of the Sedition Act, including mine. However, we do not have an alternative solution to improve relations between races," he said during Prime Minister's Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from S. Kesavan (PH-Sungai Siput), who asked why the number of cases brought to court was lower than the number of police reports lodged.
Kesavan also asked whether gaps in existing laws and the roles of different agencies required more comprehensive intervention.
Anwar said the law was subject to various interpretations, adding that investigations must be conducted transparently.
He said MPs were free to raise any weaknesses and objections.
He added that he agreed the process sometimes took too much time.
Citing cases involving alleged insults against the royal institution in Negri Sembilan, Anwar said such incidents were serious and had prompted questions over why some individuals appeared to have been exempted from action.
He said such issues were sometimes viewed through the lens of party politics or racial polemics.
"If we agree, for example, to prevent insults against religion, any religion, we will not be divided," he said.
Anwar assured MPs they could raise objections or express views on specific cases to safeguard the integrity of investigations, regardless of race or religion.
He said there was a perception that insults against other religions were tolerated while those against Islam were not.
"But if we truly safeguard harmony, do not allow insults against any religion.
"Only then can this country be safe.
"But if in all matters, including the choice of laws, we want to go by our respective religions and races, I do not think we can guarantee the safety of our country's harmony," he said.
In February, the government said it was
reviewing
the Sedition Act 1948 as part of its broader legal reform agenda.
In August, DAP national legal bureau chairman Ramkarpal Singh called for the Act to be
repealed
, backing Anwar's call to abolish colonial-era laws.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Impact Capital opens 45pct higher on ACE Market debut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Impact Capital Holdings Bhd made a strong debut on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia today, opening at 32 sen, a 45.45 per cent premium over its initial public offering (IPO) price of 22 sen.
At midday, the stock closed 6.82 per cent, or 1.5 sen to 23.5 sen. A total of 141.86 million shares changed hands, giving it a market capitalisation of RM112.8 million.
The information and communications technology (ICT) systems integrator, which specialises in critical infrastructure, raised RM21.27 million through the issuance of 96.69 million new shares at 22 sen a piece.
Another 28.62 million existing shares were offered for sale through a private placement to selected investors.
Impact Capital managing director Winston Chai Fung Chun said the listing marked an important milestone for the group after more than two decades of developing its ICT infrastructure and systems integration capabilities.
"We intend to expand our operational footprint, strengthen our workforce and business development capabilities, and enhance our technological capabilities, including through the planned Digital Innovation and Solutions Centre (DISC)," he said.
Of the IPO proceeds, RM4.67 million will be allocated for office expansion, including a planned new office in the Klang Valley to house its DISC, as well as expansions in Bintulu, Kota Kinabalu and Johor Bahru.
Another RM4.53 million will be channelled towards workforce expansion and business development initiatives, while RM2.1 million will be used to enhance its technology capabilities.
The company will allocate RM5.17 million for working capital requirements, with the remaining RM4.8 million set aside for estimated listing expenses.
Impact Capital has a track record of 21 years, providing ICT equipment and systems integration services for critical infrastructure, including telecommunications infrastructure, enterprise networks, data centres, security systems and digital twin solutions.
Its business activities also include the supply of ICT hardware and software, ICT maintenance and support, information technology service management implementation and managed network services.
Chai said the IPO will provide additional resources for the company to execute its growth plans while maintaining its focus on delivering reliable solutions and creating sustainable long-term value for shareholders.
The planned DISC will serve as a platform for solution demonstrations, customer engagement and in-house technical validation.
Public Investment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, sole underwriter and sole placement agent for the IPO.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sumatrans fear 'nobody cares' one year after floods
Article:
SWELTERING in a wooden shack in Indonesia's westernmost Aceh province, Asmiati sobs as she describes her struggle for survival in the year since flood waters swept away her home and livelihood.
Waiting on a new house promised by the government, the 63-year-old and her husband took shelter in a bare-bones hut he built himself from wood, cardboard and corrugated iron – materials donated by friends and relatives.
They are among thousands of residents of Indonesia's Sumatra island largely left to fend for themselves even as they brace for the next flood season 12 months after many lost everything.
"It was only in the very beginning that we received any aid such as rice and cooking oil," Asmiati told AFP in her remote village of Bireuen, some 200 kilometres from the provincial capital, Banda Aceh.
"I'm sad because we don't have a bed and the room is cramped. And my mind keeps going back to our home that's gone," she said, crying.
The government had promised money for residents to repair or reconstruct homes after floodwaters washed torrents of mud and logs into villages across northwest Sumatra a year ago, destroying and severely damaging more than 200,000 houses.
Some 1,200 people died and over two million were displaced.
By the government's own count, 11 months later, fewer than a quarter of eligible people have received their promised dues – ranging from 15 million to 70 million rupiah (US$820-US$3,800) per household.
[[nid:1584580]]
Fewer than 2,000 houses of about 50,000 needed in the hardest-hit Aceh province have been constructed, Safrizal Zakaria Ali, the head of a regional government reconstruction task force, told AFP.
In 11 months, government agents have constructed part of the foundation for Asmiati's new home on the land where her old one once stood.
She and her husband Hendrik Ginting, 53, both lost jobs in the construction industry rendered obsolete by the expansive flood damage.
The pomelo garden with which Asmiati had augmented her household income was washed away along with all the couple's possessions.
Since January, they have shared the wooden hut with four other family members. They cook and do their ablutions outdoors.
"I feel disappointed in the government... It's like nobody cares about us," said Asmiati, who now brings in under $3 a day making brooms from coconut fibres.
In Mesidah, a five-hour drive from Bireuen, villagers banded together to fix a damaged road that used to connect 14 villages and is crucial for transporting crops during the harvest season.
Since September, they pooled some 80 million rupiah (more than US$4,300) in donations, using it to buy concrete, gravel, sand and a compacting machine.
"About 700 residents helped with the work. From morning 'til night, they kept at it," resident Sukiran told AFP of the makeshift road that, for the moment, can only hold motorcycles, not cars.
"We refuse to stay beaten down and complacent. We help one another," said Sukiran, who like many Indonesians uses one name.
Residents of the same village had also erected a temporary bamboo pedestrian and motorcycle bridge to replace a concrete one washed away by the floods.
[[nid:1584579]]
They used it for eight months until the government built a new one.
"Our area was isolated and no-one noticed. That's why we took the initiative to build whatever we could. We did not wait," said Sukiran.
The government in Jakarta has allocated a three-year budget of more than 100 trillion rupiah (some US$5.5 billion) for post-flood rehabilitation in three provinces of Sumatra.
"We're working hard to fix everything, and thank God, for the past few months, many areas in Aceh, West Sumatra, and North Sumatra have already recovered," President Prabowo Subianto said on a visit to the area this month.
But residents and critics say help has been too slow to come.
For one, the government should be focusing on dredging sediment from rivers and repairing embankments "so that disasters do not keep happening," Alfian, spokesman for the Aceh-Sumatra Civil Society Coalition for Disaster Concern, told AFP.
Safrizal, the task force head, pointed to the enormity of the reconstruction challenge, with hundreds of bridges and roads damaged or destroyed on top of tens of thousands of homes.
It was also not easy to find land in flood safe zones for housing reconstruction, he said.
The government was working as fast as it can but "the public must understand that this work is... gradual," he told AFP in Banda Aceh.
As the rainy season returns after a prolonged El Nino-driven drought, fears of another disaster are growing.
"Whenever the rain starts pouring down... a feeling of unease arises in my heart. We feel afraid even inside the house," a survivor of last year's disaster, Arsan Arben, said in Mesidah.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: At least two dead, six injured in explosion in Vietnam's capital [WATCH]
Article:
HANOI: At least two people were killed and six others injured after an explosion caused a two-storey eatery to collapse in Vietnam's capital, Hanoi, on Tuesday morning, Xinhua reported, citing local media outlet VnExpress.
The blast occurred at around 8am local time at a porridge restaurant on Nguyen Van Tuyet Street. The restaurant was open and serving customers at the time.
The blast reportedly originated near the gas stove in the kitchen, VnExpress reported.
About 10 houses and other buildings across the street, roughly 15 metres from the blast site, were also damaged.
Debris was scattered along a stretch of road more than 20 metres long, and several motorbikes were knocked over.
The cause of the explosion is under investigation.

Title: Suffian Abdullah takes over as new Kuala Lumpur traffic police chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Assistant Commissioner Suffian Abdullah has been appointed Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief, effective today.
He succeeds Senior Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa, who has been appointed principal assistant director (General Policing) at Bukit Aman's Internal Security and Public Order Department.
The handover ceremony was held at the Kuala Lumpur police station parade ground and witnessed by Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus.
The ceremony began with the rank-pinning ceremony, followed by the signing and exchange of handing-over documents between Suffian and Zamzuri.
Fadil thanked Zamzuri for his service and leadership during his nearly three years as department chief.
He said Zamzuri had helped ensure smooth traffic management, strengthen enforcement and address road safety issues in the capital.
Fadil said leading a department responsible for traffic management in a metropolitan city such as Kuala Lumpur required firm leadership, sound decision-making and the ability to balance enforcement with public interests.
He also congratulated Suffian on his appointment, expressing confidence that his experience and leadership would help maintain the department's performance and introduce improvements to meet current challenges.
"I believe that with his experience, knowledge and leadership capabilities, Suffian will be able to uphold the department's excellence while introducing improvements suited to current needs and challenges.
"I hope all Kuala Lumpur TEID officers and personnel will extend their full support, cooperation and commitment to the new leadership to ensure the department's plans and agendas are successfully implemented," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pope Francis revealed in personal diary having seen devil
Article:
VATICAN CITY: The late Pope Francis saw the devil three times and once saw the "gates of hell", he revealed in his personal diary, excerpts of which were published on Tuesday in a new book.
"The Private Diary of Pope Francis", by Argentine Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, includes passages taken from a journal the former Jorge Bergoglio kept between 1992 and 2024. The document reveals his worries, regrets and self-critiques — as well as his enormous humanity and faith.
Fernandez, head of the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, said he was asked by Francis to help make known to the world the musings inside the black plastic journal.
Upon Francis's death last year, Fernandez expressed concern to his successor, Leo XIV, that the book would be "left forgotten in some storage". He was allowed to publish passages, noting that "the spiritual concerns present in his (Francis's) heart are very clear and can do us good".
In one of the most intriguing revelations, Francis writes that while archbishop of Buenos Aires, he saw the devil on three separate occasions, including "from the car while I was going home, and in the choir during the mass", and once in Rome following a visit to Chile.
"I discovered that the demon was prowling brazenly, hovering cunningly," wrote Francis in his journal on Jan 24, 2021, according to an advance copy of the French-language version of the book published by Albin Michel and viewed by AFP.
Francis wrote that he recalled three episodes "where I'm sure he actually appeared physically".
"About 15 years ago. I saw him from the car window. I won't forget his threatening and, at the same time, alluring eyes," he wrote.
During the second episode inside a Carmelite chapel, Francis wrote: "He looked at me with flaming eyes.
"I won't forget that look, more intense than the previous one. They were like flashes of fire."
The third episode occurred during a meeting in Rome, following a visit to Chile.
"I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything... I can't forget the powerful rasp of his voice," he wrote, adding that "the Lord gave me the chance to free myself from these encounters".
Francis also revealed, on June 7, 2018, that the night before, while getting ready to go to sleep, he "saw the gates of hell".
"Pagan seduction in all its force. I watched a little, and it terrified me," he said, adding that he "took the rosary as a weapon".
"It's dangerous to get close to the gates of hell, because flames can spring out and burn," he wrote.
SELF-CRITICISM
Throughout the diary, Francis does not hesitate to criticise himself, for his occasional "feelings of disdain, envy, pride" or for having ignored a drunk man in the street who addressed him "because I wanted to walk in peace and quiet".
"The arrogant, self-sufficient, cynical Jorge who lies to himself," is how the former pope described himself on Dec 30, 2022.
On Jan 15, 2017, he confessed that "for the past three or four days, I've been really angry and upset".
While charismatic, Pope Francis also had a strong personality and was sometimes criticised within the Curia, the Catholic Church's governing body, for being authoritarian.
Mercy is a recurrent theme in the journal.
"In hindsight, I realised all the harm I've caused in my life. How much of the Lord's mercy I need!" he wrote on Jan 5, 1997.
END OF LIFE
Pope Francis appeared to worry that his days on Earth would be short-lived, fretting over his ageing and the need to "deal with it".
In 1996, at age 60 — nearly three decades before his death — he wrote: "I want to do good with the little time I have left, hoping to be kind.
"How much time wasted, how much harm done!"
In 2001, he wrote that "the age of 65 makes me think of the end. I'm already counting down".
The worries continued even after becoming pope in 2013, with Francis writing on Apr 9, 2016, that "the devil's attacks, in different forms, have increased... Is this a sign that time is running out and he doesn't want to lose?"
The journal contains 86 pages written before his election as pope in 2013, and another 55 afterwards.
One of the briefest — and most moving — passages in Francis's diary comes on July 21, 2013: "On March 13, they elected me pope."
Francis died on Apr 21, 2025.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ECRL nears finish line with 99.03pct completion, KotaSAS station opens
Article:
KUANTAN: The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), is less than one per cent away from completion ahead of its launch on Dec 12.
Chief Secretary to the Government and Malaysia Rail Link (MRL) chairman Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said construction of the first phase, linking Kota Baru, Kelantan, to Gombak, Selangor, had reached 99.03 per cent completion.
"The project is now entering its final stage of preparations ahead of the targeted commencement of commercial services on Dec 12.
"The 258km ECRL alignment in Pahang was 99.17 per cent complete as of last month," he said at the opening of the KotaSAS station here today.
The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, officiated the opening of the station, the
first of 16
along the ECRL's first phase between Gombak Integrated Transport Terminal and Kota Baru.
Shamsul Azri said the ECRL was expected to boost Pahang's economy by attracting trade, investment and tourism, while creating employment opportunities.
He said the passenger service would connect Kuantan to Gombak in one hour and 30 minutes, halving the journey time compared with the nearly three-hour drive.
"The project will also spur economic development through
Transit-Oriented Development (TOD)
, an urban planning concept that integrates residential, commercial and public amenities around transport hubs, including bus and railway stations," he said.
Pahang will have seven ECRL stations. Cherating and KotaSAS will serve passengers only, while Kuantan Port City, Paya Besar, Maran, Temerloh and Bentong will handle both passenger and cargo services.
On the KotaSAS station, Shamsul Azri said the 15.57ha site had been developed as Pahang's main railway station, with architecture inspired by the state's royal heritage.
He said its design incorporated crossed elephant tusks from the Pahang coat of arms, symbolising royal customs and the historical role of elephants as ceremonial transport for the royal household.
The station is equipped with a VIP guest room, waiting areas, staff quarters, pedestrian walkways and designated pick-up and drop-off zones for buses and e-hailing services.
It also has more than 500 parking bays, including covered spaces fitted with solar panels.
Located near the Sultan Ahmad Shah Administrative Centre and the state mosque, which is nearing completion, the station is expected to serve as a major transport hub for the state capital and support KotaSAS's development.
The 665km ECRL runs through Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Selangor. Its first phase is scheduled to begin operations next month, with ticket sales expected to open soon.
The second phase, extending the line from Gombak to Port Klang, is expected to begin operations by January 2028.
Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, Tengku Mahkota of Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah Ibni Al-Sultan Abdullah, MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak and Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman's final gift: Family donates her heart, lungs and liver
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A woman who died on Sunday after being in a coma following an accident in Kluang gave others the gift if life after her family agreed to donate her heart, lungs and liver.
Nurul Natasya Ahmad Jaafar, who had been in a coma for several days following the accident on Nov 19, died at Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) on Nov 22.
Her family's decision to donate her organs turned their personal tragedy into hope for patients awaiting life-saving transplants.
HSA paid a final tribute to Nurul Natasya through a
'Walk of Honour'
.
Doctors and medical personnel lined the hospital corridors as the organ donor was wheeled out of the hospital, with green lights illuminating the building to symbolise gratitude and respect for her
final gift of life
.
The Fire and Rescue Department coordinated the organ donation mission yesterday.
The department sent a helicopter to transport the organs from HSA to Subang before they were taken to the National Heart Institute (IJN) in Kuala Lumpur.
The mission was led by fire officer Sofian Ahmed, assisted by Zulkhaire Zabidi, two crew members and four Health Ministry medical personnel.
In a Facebook post, the department said the helicopter, based at the northern region air base in Bertam, Penang, arrived at HSA at 9.22am.
HSA described Nurul Natasya's sacrifice as a powerful reminder that one person's final act of kindness could give others another chance at life.
Her passing also drew an outpouring of condolences and tributes on social media, with many describing the family's decision as an enduring act of charity.
Nurul Natasya was buried at the Kampung Cahaya Baru Muslim cemetery in Masai yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perak tables record-high RM1.693b budget for 2027
Article:
IPOH: The state government has tabled a record RM1.693 billion state budget for 2027, the largest allocation in the state's history, with RM593 million set aside for development expenditure.
Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the budget was formulated as a continuation of the development agenda under the Perak Sejahtera 2030 Plan, with the state government prioritising the well-being of the people and sustainable development.
He said the budget also carried a projected deficit of RM128 million, taking into account the need to finance the state's development agenda and various programmes planned for the people's well-being.
"However, experience over the past several years has shown that a projected deficit does not necessarily reflect the state's actual financial position at the end of the year," he said when tabling the Perak 2027 Budget at the state legislative assembly.
Saarani said the state government projected RM1.565 billion in revenue and development receipts, an increase of RM47 million compared with 2026.
"The amount comprised RM719 million in tax revenue, RM554 million in non-tax revenue, RM250 million in non-revenue receipts and RM42 million in development receipts."
Of the total expenditure, he said RM1.1 billion would be allocated for operating expenditure, while RM593 million would be channelled towards development expenditure.
"The development allocation represents an increase of RM25 million, or 4.4 per cent, compared with the previous year, and is also the highest allocation in the history of the state budget," he said.
He said the increased development allocation would provide greater room for the state government to continue infrastructure projects, strengthen public amenities, stimulate economic activities and implement development initiatives that were priorities for the people.
He said the operating expenditure allocation comprised RM508.2 million for emoluments, RM393.7 million for services and supplies, RM12.3 million for asset purchases, RM179.1 million for grants and fixed payments, and RM6.6 million for other expenditure.
"The increase also took into account annual salary increments for civil servants, overtime claims and the creation of new positions at the Perak Drainage and Irrigation Department," he said.
He said efficient revenue collection, prudent prioritisation and firm expenditure controls would remain the foundation of the state's fiscal management.
"Fiscal discipline does not mean restricting development, but ensuring that every ringgit spent delivers meaningful returns to the people," he said.
Meanwhile, he said the 2027 Budget carried the theme "Prosperous Perak, Thriving People: Delivering Results, Building Confidence".
He said the theme reflected the state government's determination to translate the progress achieved into tangible benefits for the people while strengthening public confidence in the state's future.
The budget would be driven by five main focuses: people's well-being; governance of state-strategic projects; human capital and youth development; environmental sustainability; and food supply security.
Saarani said the five focuses would guide the state government in determining spending priorities, strengthening public services and amenities, expediting development projects and expanding economic opportunities for the people.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KL traffic enforcement up 26.8pct, 197 killed in 67,262 accidents, teenage arrests surge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (TEID) recorded 563,953 enforcement actions between January and October this year, a 26.8 per cent increase from the 444,594 recorded during the corresponding period last year.
The enforcement actions comprised summonses and notices issued, arrests made and vehicles seized.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the enforcement actions were recorded through five major operations, namely Op Pematuhan, Op Perdagangan, Op Khas Bersepadu, Op Motosikal and Op Mabuk.
Fadil said 3,702 operations were conducted in the first 10 months of this year, with Op Pematuhan accounting for the highest number, followed by Op Khas Bersepadu and Op Motosikal.
He said 990 arrests were also recorded during the period for offences under Sections 45A, 42 and 50(3) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"This shows that TEID's enforcement and investigative efforts are not only focused on ordinary traffic offences but also serious offences that could endanger the safety of road users," he said at the Kuala Lumpur TEID chief's rank-pinning and handover of duties ceremony.
However, Fadil expressed concern over the persistently high number of road accidents, with 67,262 cases recorded between January and October this year.
These involved 197 deaths, 63 cases of serious injuries and 1,842 cases of minor injuries, while another 65,160 cases involved vehicle damage.
"Although the number of accidents recorded between January and October 2026 is lower than the total recorded in 2025, this cannot yet be regarded as an achievement as the reporting period for this year has yet to cover the entire year," he said.
He said the number of fatal accidents involving drink-driving had also increased to four in the first 10 months of this year, compared with three throughout last year.
He called on Kuala Lumpur TEID to intensify road safety advocacy programmes, increase monitoring at high-risk locations and strengthen enforcement against offences that could lead to accidents.
Fadil also highlighted the need to pay particular attention to traffic offences involving teenagers, especially underage schoolchildren.
He said the number of schoolchildren aged below 17 arrested under Section 42 of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous driving had more than doubled since 2024.
A total of 52 schoolchildren were arrested in 2024, rising to 69 last year before increasing to 114 in the first 10 months of this year.
"This increase is not merely an enforcement issue but also involves education, awareness, parental supervision and the collective responsibility of society," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's labour productivity growth slows to 4.4pct in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's labour productivity growth has moderated to 4.4 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 from 5.5 per cent in the preceding quarter, amid slower growth in output per hour worked.
The Statistics Department said labour productivity, measured by value added per hour worked, rose to RM48.20 in the quarter from RM46.60 a year earlier.
The growth was supported by a 5.5 per cent expansion in the economy, while total hours worked increased by 1.0 per cent to 9.7 billion hours.
Labour productivity measured by value added per employed person also moderated, growing by 4.2 per cent compared with 4.9 per cent in the second quarter.
Value added per employed person increased to RM27,788 from RM26,598, while total employment rose by 1.2 per cent to 16.8 million people.
At the sectoral level, manufacturing recorded the strongest labour productivity growth per hour worked at 6.9 per cent, although this was slightly lower than the 7.1 per cent recorded in the preceding quarter.
Construction followed with growth of 6.4 per cent, accelerating from 5.6 per cent previously, while services expanded by 4.2 per cent compared with 5.4 per cent in the second quarter.
Agriculture returned to positive territory, recording growth of 1.9 per cent against a contraction of 4.4 per cent previously.
However, mining and quarrying productivity contracted by 5.0 per cent, reversing the 9.1 per cent growth recorded in the preceding quarter.
A similar trend was observed in productivity measured by value added per employed person, with manufacturing leading sectoral growth at 7.4 per cent, compared with 7.3 per cent previously.
Construction expanded by 5.4 per cent, down from 6.0 per cent, while services grew by 4.1 per cent against 4.2 per cent in the second quarter.
Agriculture recorded a 0.7 per cent expansion, reversing a 3.7 per cent contraction in the preceding quarter.
Mining and quarrying remained the weakest performer, with productivity contracting by 5.5 per cent after growing by 9.2 per cent in the previous quarter.
The department said the improvement in labour productivity reflected the economy's capacity to generate higher output amid external uncertainties.
It added that greater emphasis on high-value-added activities, efficient resource utilisation and innovation-led growth would be essential to sustaining productivity gains.
These efforts are in line with the objectives of the 13th Malaysia Plan and are expected to strengthen the country's economic resilience and support national productivity growth targets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Digital connectivity must be matched by greater responsibility
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Responsible use of digital technology, fact-checking and personal accountability are key to creating a safer online environment, said Media Prima Bhd News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim.
She said the rapid spread of misinformation, AI-generated content and online harm highlighted the need for greater awareness and responsibility.
"The digital world has given all of us a voice. But the important question is: are we using that voice responsibly?
"Information travels faster than ever, with news reaching millions within minutes and photographs going viral before their authenticity can be verified.
"A single social media post can influence public opinion and affect someone's reputation. This is a reminder that while technology has democratised communication, the power it brings also carries serious responsibility," she said in her speech at the Communication and Media Festival (Commed) 2026, held at Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) here today.
Also present were Faculty of Communication and Media Studies (FKPM) dean Prof Dr Abd Rasid Abd Rahman, deputy dean (research and industry) Associate Prof Dr Tengku Elena Tengku Mahamad, and Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) chief executive officer Mediha Mahmood.
Drawing on her journalism experience, Farrah Naz, who is also New Straits Times group editor and an adjunct professor at the faculty, said technology had transformed how news was gathered, verified, produced and delivered, but the fundamental principles of journalism remained unchanged.
She said news production had always involved rigorous processes, including gathering information, checking facts, consulting sources and editorial scrutiny.
"Back then, we had all the time in the world to gather information, speak to sources, check and recheck facts, consult editors and undergo editorial scrutiny before a story reached the public.
"Today, the pressure is very different. Newsrooms operate in an environment where speed is highly valued, with audiences expecting updates almost instantly.
"Digital platforms reward engagement, and sometimes the pressure to be first can be overwhelming.
"But let me emphasise one important lesson from the newsroom: being first means very little if you are wrong."
She said information, once published and circulated, could take on a life of its own, making accuracy and verification more important than ever.
"Even when a correction is issued, screenshots and reposts can continue circulating long after the original information has been corrected or the post taken down.
"That is why verification remains fundamental to responsible journalism. This principle should not apply only to journalists but to everyone in the industry."
Farrah Naz also called for caution before sharing or commenting on information online, stressing that digital interactions could have real-world consequences.
"Before sharing a sensational headline, ask whether it is true. Before forwarding an alarming message, check your source.
"Before commenting on someone's personal tragedy or misfortune, consider the human being behind the screen.
"Every digital interaction involves real people, real emotions and real consequences. It is also important to understand the very real legal implications of our actions online."
On the festival's theme, "CTRL + THINK: Taking Control of Our Digital World", she said people needed to exercise control over what they consumed, shared and how they responded online.
She also highlighted the growing influence of artificial intelligence, describing it as both an opportunity and a responsibility for future media professionals.
While AI could improve efficiency and creativity, she said it could not replace human judgement, ethics and professional accountability.
"We must never allow technology to do the thinking for us," she said.
he also emphasised that credibility remained the media industry's most valuable asset, urging students to embrace digital innovation without compromising professional ethics and integrity.
"Be technologically competent, but remain intellectually curious. Strive to be influential, but always be responsible," she said.
The two-day Commed 2026 features forums, workshops, masterclasses, interactive games, exhibition booths and sessions with industry professionals, alumni and strategic partners.
Visitors can also take part in an interactive digital safety workshop conducted by the Content Forum and visit exhibition booths at the foyer of Menara Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor tightens licensing rules to curb 'Ali Baba' businesses
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor is considering three additional licensing conditions to prevent foreigners from illegally operating businesses through local licence holders.
The measures target 'Ali Baba' arrangements, where Malaysians rent out or allow foreigners to use their business licences to bypass restrictions on foreign business ownership.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the proposed conditions would prioritise Malaysians as cashiers at retail outlets, require foreign workers to have valid passports and work permits, and require business owners to submit updated lists of foreign employees to local authorities.
Jafni said the state government was reviewing licensing guidelines across all 16 local authorities to standardise requirements and enforcement while protecting business opportunities for Malaysians.
"From 2025 to September this year, enforcement operations by the 16 local authorities resulted in 1,092 seizures, 211 notices and 511 compounds, with the compounds totalling RM324,500. The offences involved foreigners operating businesses without licences."
Jafni said foreigners had not been issued hawker licences to operate at morning, night or farmers' markets.
"Licences issued to Malaysians are not meant to be rented out, surrendered or transferred to foreigners. Any misuse will result in stern action, including licence cancellation, subject to existing laws," he said during the state assembly sitting at Kota Iskandar today.
He was responding to questions from Selamat Takim (BN-Sungai Balang), Baharudin Mohamed Taib (BN-Permas) and Anuar Abd Manap (BN-Pemanis) on the growing presence of foreigners, including those operating businesses illegally.
Jafni said the state government was also studying amendments to local authorities' Trade, Business and Industrial by-laws to strengthen controls and action against licence abuse.
It had also proposed that local authorities identify 290 business activity hotspots for targeted monitoring and enforcement.
These comprise 90 areas under three city councils, 140 under seven municipal councils and 60 under six district councils.
Monthly integrated enforcement operations involving local authorities, the Immigration Department, police, the Labour Department and relevant technical agencies were also being proposed.
"Enforcement must not be seasonal or triggered only when an issue goes viral. Action must be firm, consistent and continuous," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Macquarie-led consortium buys Edotco assets for US$1.2bil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Macquarie Asset Management is leading a consortium to buy the international telecommunications tower businesses of Edotco Group Sdn Bhd across five Asia Pacific markets in a deal valued at about US$1.2 billion (RM5.0 billion).
The transaction involves a coordinated acquisition of Edotco's assets across five jurisdictions.
Macquarie Asia-Pacific Infrastructure Fund 4 (MAIF4) is taking over its Philippine operations, while other consortium members will acquire the businesses in the remaining four markets.
The Philippine business, Edotco Towers Inc, owns and operates about 3,200 telecommunications towers that support the country's mobile network operators.
The platform had a tenancy ratio of about 1.2 times as at June 30, 2026, providing room to accommodate additional tenants as demand for mobile connectivity and data consumption grows.
Macquarie Asset said it had structured the transaction as a single coordinated solution, allowing Edotco Group's shareholders to pursue the divestment of their complex regional portfolio while giving the consortium a foothold in the Philippine telecommunications tower market.
Macquarie Group Asia chief executive and Macquarie Asset Management Asia-Pacific Infrastructure co-head Verena Lim said the acquisition reflected the group's confidence in the growth of digital infrastructure across Southeast Asia.
"Edotco Philippines is an established platform with an important role in supporting the country's growing connectivity needs.
"The investment reflects our conviction in the continued growth of digital infrastructure across Southeast Asia, and our ability to draw on our regional presence, local relationships and infrastructure expertise to execute complex opportunities across markets," she said.
The transaction is subject to customary conditions, including regulatory and shareholder approvals, and is expected to be completed in 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sheikh Hasina seeks to return to Bangladesh on Dec 16 on state carrier
Article:
NEW DELHI: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on Dec 16, the anniversary of the end of her country's 1971 liberation war with Pakistan, her spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday, though the government said she could only return through extradition.
It is the first time Hasina, 79, has set a specific date for her return, potentially raising political and legal tensions in a country where her party is banned and violence has risen since she sought a new passport and other documents earlier this month.
In addition to seeking the paperwork, which was cancelled months after she fled to Delhi following the uprising against her, Hasina has urged the Bangladeshi government to arrange her return on flag carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
"Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on Aug 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," the spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, said in a statement.
"Having exiled her contrary to the Constitution under such circumstances, it is now the responsibility of the government to make possible her return to Bangladesh on Victory Day on Dec 16th."
The government, however, reiterated that she could only be extradited by India, having been sentenced to death by a Bangladeshi court last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising. Hasina has denied the charges from exile.
"Hasina is a convicted criminal; a fugitive terrorist," Humaiun Kobir, Bangladesh's minister of state for foreign affairs, told Reuters.
"She can only return home by extradition treaty; in handcuffs, and under strict surveillance."
India's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In April, the ministry said it was examining Bangladesh's request to extradite her and that it wanted to "engage constructively with the new government and further strengthen bilateral ties".
On the request to arrange a flight, Kobir said: "Bangladesh will not entertain any such delusional request."
Aminul Islam, chief prosecutor of Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal, which sentenced Hasina to death, said it was unreasonable for a convicted fugitive to expect the government to arrange her return.
A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would be arrested and jailed on her return and that there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring her back.
The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced her out of power.

Title: PM: Govt takes over refugee registration from UNHCR
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Only refugee registrations administered by the Immigration Department and Home Ministry will be recognised as valid under a cabinet decision to tighten refugee management in Malaysia.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was taking over the registration function from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) amid concerns that its registration procedures were too lenient and complicated the work of Malaysian authorities.
He said the authorities needed to distinguish genuine refugees from individuals entering the country through syndicates, including criminal networks.
"Registration will no longer be handled by UNHCR because the registration process was too easy and complicated our work.
"Some are refugees, while others enter through syndicates, including criminal syndicates.
"If we recognise all of them as refugees, the country cannot be managed properly.
"That is why the cabinet has decided that valid registration will come exclusively under the Immigration Department and Home Ministry," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar was responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa (BN-Tampin) on the government's policy direction following the introduction of the Refugee Registration Document (DPP).
On employment opportunities for refugees, Anwar said priority would continue to be given to Malaysians.
However, he said relevant government departments could consider special appeals involving refugees with specialised skills or expertise not available among locals.
"Priority is given to locals.
"However, in certain cases involving specialised skills or expertise not possessed by Malaysians, I believe the relevant departments can consider special appeals," he said.
Anwar said the government would continue diplomatic negotiations to address the refugee situation, with resolving domestic challenges remaining its priority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Interstate housebreaking gang linked to RM293,500 losses busted
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have crippled an interstate housebreaking gang linked to 15 cases involving losses estimated at RM293,500, following the arrest of two men less than an hour after their latest break-in.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the gang was believed to have targeted unguarded homes during the day in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Perak and Pahang.
He said the Bukit Aman CID Intelligence and Operations Division (D4) arrested the two local men, aged 40 and 44, at 1pm on Nov 16 under Op Pintu Kit.
The suspects were arrested while travelling in a vehicle in Taman City, Kuala Lumpur.
"Preliminary investigations revealed that both suspects were believed to have been involved in a housebreaking at Taman Rainbow, Jalan Ipoh, around noon on the same day.
"The arrests were made less than an hour after the incident was reported," he said in a statement today.
Police seized a black Toyota Camry fitted with false registration plates, stolen items and housebreaking tools.
The seized items included mobile phones, tablets, watches, laptops, a closed-circuit television (CCTV) system, three sets of vehicle registration plates, RM1,000 in cash, four Touch 'n Go cards and a gold purchase receipt.
Bags, shoes, clothing, gloves and face masks believed to have been used in the break-ins were also seized.
Kumar said one suspect had 67 previous criminal and drug-related offences, including 41 for housebreaking, while the other had two criminal and three drug-related offences.
The first suspect also tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
He said police had identified another gang member who remained at large and were tracking him down.
The arrests enabled police to solve seven housebreaking cases in Selangor, five in Perak, two in Pahang and one in Kuala Lumpur.
He said the gang's modus operandi involved using vehicles with false registration plates and targeted unguarded terrace houses during the day when occupants were away.
Members would force their way into homes and were also believed to have used modified equipment to gain access to properties fitted with automatic gates.
Both suspects have been remanded until Nov 27 to facilitate investigations under Section 457 of the Penal Code for housebreaking.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of 14 years if the intended offence is theft. Repeat offenders may also be fined or whipped.
Kumar advised homeowners to install additional locks and CCTV cameras, keep valuables in secure locations and alert police to suspicious individuals or vehicles in residential areas.
